units.zh: 列傳一百二十二
units.en: Biographies 122
units.literal: Biographies, Number 122

units.zh: 富僧阿伊勒圖胡貴俞金鼇尹德禧剛塔
units.en: Fu Senga, Yi Leitu, Hu Gui, Yu Jin'ao, Yin Dexi, and Gangta
units.literal: Fu Senga, Yi Leitu, Hu Gui, Yu Jin'ao, Yin Dexi, Gangta

units.zh: 富僧阿，舒穆祿氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
units.en: Fu Senga, of the Sumulu clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
units.literal: Fu Senga, of the Sumulu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

units.zh: 雍正初，授拜唐阿，累遷頭等侍衛。
units.en: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was made a palace attendant and rose in due course to First Class Bodyguard.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Yongzheng reign he was appointed a baitangga and was repeatedly promoted to First Class Bodyguard.

units.zh: 出為副都統，歷成都、三姓、寧古塔諸地。
units.en: He was then posted as deputy military governor, serving in turn at Chengdu, Sanxing, Ningguta, and elsewhere.
units.literal: He went out to serve as deputy military governor, successively at Chengdu, Sanxing, Ningguta, and other posts.

units.zh: 擢將軍，自荊州移黑龍江。
units.en: Promoted to frontier general, he was moved from Jingzhou to Heilongjiang.
units.literal: He was promoted to general and transferred from Jingzhou to Heilongjiang.

units.zh: 黑龍江北鄰俄羅斯，康熙二十九年與定界。
units.en: Heilongjiang's northern frontier adjoins Russia; the border had been delimited in the twenty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign.
units.literal: Heilongjiang on the north borders Russia; in the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi the boundary was fixed.

units.zh: 歲久，將吏憚行邊，道裡不能詳。
units.en: Over time the garrison officers grew reluctant to patrol the frontier, and the routes and distances were no longer known with precision.
units.literal: As years passed, officers and clerks feared traveling the border, and the routes and distances could not be known in detail.

units.zh: 富僧阿遣副都統瑚爾起等分探諸水源，皆至興堪山還報。
units.en: Fu Senga dispatched Deputy Military Governor Hu'erqi and others to reconnoiter the various headwaters in separate parties; each party reached Xingkan Mountain and returned with its report.
units.literal: Fu Senga sent the deputy military governor Hu'erqi and others to explore the various river sources separately; all reached Xingkanshan and returned to report.

units.zh: 乃上疏言：「副都統瑚爾起探格爾畢齊河源，自黑龍江至格爾畢齊河口，水程一千六百九十七里；
units.en: He then memorialized the throne, reporting: "Deputy Military Governor Hu'erqi traced the Ge'erbiji River to its source: from the Heilongjiang to the Ge'erbiji estuary the water route measures 1,697 li;
units.literal: He then submitted a memorial stating: "Deputy Military Governor Hu'erqi explored the source of the Ge'erbiji River; from the Heilongjiang to the mouth of the Ge'erbiji, the water route is 1,697 li;

units.zh: 自河口行陸路二百四十七里，至興堪山：其間無人跡。
units.en: from the estuary a land march of 247 li reaches Xingkan Mountain; the country between is utterly uninhabited.
units.literal: from the mouth by land route 247 li to Xingkanshan: in between there are no human traces.

units.zh: 協領納林布探精奇哩江源，自黑龍江入精奇哩江，北行至托克河口，水程一千五百八十七里；
units.en: Assistant Commandant Nalinbu reconnoitered the Jingqiri headwaters: entering the Jingqiri from the Heilongjiang and sailing north to the Tuo estuary, the water route is 1,587 li;
units.literal: Assistant Commandant Nalinbu explored the source of the Jingqiri River; entering the Jingqiri from the Heilongjiang and proceeding north to the mouth of the Tuo River, the water route is 1,587 li;

units.zh: 自河口行陸路二百四十里至興堪山：地苦寒，無水草禽獸。
units.en: from the estuary a land march of 240 li reaches Xingkan Mountain; the region is bitterly cold and devoid of pasture, waterfowl, or game.
units.literal: from the mouth by land route 240 li to Xingkanshan: the land is bitterly cold, without water, grass, birds, or beasts.

units.zh: 協領偉保探西里木第河源，自黑龍江經精奇哩江入西里木第河口，復過英肯河，水程一千三百五里；
units.en: Assistant Commandant Weibao traced the Xilimudi headwaters: from the Heilongjiang through the Jingqiri into the Xilimudi estuary, then past the Yingken River, the water route is 1,305 li;
units.literal: Assistant Commandant Weibao explored the source of the Xilimudi River; from the Heilongjiang via the Jingqiri into the mouth of the Xilimudi, then crossing the Yingken River, the water route is 1,305 li;

units.zh: 自英肯河口行陸路一百八十里至興堪山：地苦寒，無水草禽獸。
units.en: from the Yingken estuary a land march of 180 li reaches Xingkan Mountain; there too the country is bitterly cold and without pasture or wildlife.
units.literal: from the mouth of the Yingken by land route 180 li to Xingkanshan: the land is bitterly cold, without water, grass, birds, or beasts.

units.zh: 協領阿迪木保探鈕曼河源，自黑龍江入鈕曼河，復經西里木第河入烏默勒河口，水程一千六百十五里；
units.en: Assistant Commandant Adimubao reconnoitered the Niuman headwaters: entering the Niuman from the Heilongjiang, then via the Xilimudi to the Wumole estuary, the water route is 1,615 li;
units.literal: Assistant Commandant Adimubao explored the source of the Niuman River; entering the Niuman from the Heilongjiang, then via the Xilimudi into the mouth of the Wumole, the water route is 1,615 li;

units.zh: 自河口行陸路四百五十六里至興堪山。
units.en: from the estuary a land march of 456 li reaches Xingkan Mountain.
units.literal: from the mouth by land route 456 li to Xingkanshan.

units.zh: 諸地俱無俄羅斯偷越。
units.en: Along all these routes there was no sign of Russians crossing the border illicitly.
units.literal: In all these regions there was no Russian trespass.

units.zh: 臣按呼倫貝爾有額爾古訥河，西為俄羅斯界，東屬我國。
units.en: Your subject observes that in Hulunbuir the Ergun River marks the frontier: its west bank is Russian territory, its east bank our own.
units.literal: Your subject notes that in Hulunbuir there is the Ergun River; to the west is the Russian border, to the east it belongs to our state.

units.zh: 自此至珠爾特，處處設卡。
units.en: From that point to Zhu'erte, guard posts have been established at intervals throughout.
units.literal: From there to Zhu'erte, checkpoints are set everywhere.

units.zh: 今復自珠爾特至莫哩勒克河口，設卡二，索博爾罕增立鄂博，逐日巡查。
units.en: It is now proposed to add two more posts between Zhu'erte and the Molileke estuary, to erect additional border cairns in Sobo'erhan, and to inspect the line daily.
units.literal: Now again from Zhu'erte to the mouth of the Molileke, two checkpoints are set; in Sobo'erhan additional obos are erected, with daily patrols.

units.zh: 俄羅斯、鼐瑪爾斷難偷越。
units.en: Russians and Naimar tribesmen will scarcely be able to slip across undetected.
units.literal: Russians and Naimar will certainly find it difficult to cross secretly.

units.zh: 黑龍江與俄羅斯接壤，興堪山延亙至海。
units.en: Along the Heilongjiang our territory adjoins Russia, and Xingkan Mountain runs in an unbroken line to the coast.
units.literal: Heilongjiang borders Russia; Xingkanshan extends continuously to the sea.

units.zh: 嗣後請飭打牲總管每歲六月遣章京、驍騎校、兵丁，自水路與捕貂人同至托克、英肯兩河口，及鄂勒希、西里木第兩河間，巡察還報；
units.en: Henceforth the Fur Tribute superintendent should each year in the sixth month dispatch clerks, cavalry officers, and troops by boat, together with sable hunters, to the Tuo and Yingken estuaries and to the stretch between the E'lexi and Xilimudi rivers, patrol the ground, and report back;
units.literal: Hereafter it is requested to order the Fur Tribute superintendent each year in the sixth month to dispatch zhangjing, darti-achas, and soldiers, by water route together with sable hunters to the two river mouths of Tuo and Yingken, and between the two rivers E'lexi and Xilimudi, to patrol and return to report;

units.zh: 三年遣副總管、佐領、驍騎校於冰解後，自水路至興堪山巡察還報；
units.en: every three years, after the ice breaks, deputy superintendents, company captains, and cavalry officers should travel by water to Xingkan Mountain, patrol, and return with their reports;
units.literal: every three years dispatch deputy superintendents, zuolings, and darti-achas after the ice breaks, by water route to Xingkanshan to patrol and return to report;

units.zh: 黑龍江官兵每歲巡察格爾畢齊河口，三年亦至興堪山巡察還報：歲終報部。」
units.en: Heilongjiang troops should inspect the Ge'erbiji estuary annually and reach Xingkan Mountain on the triennial circuit; all findings are to be reported to the Board at year's end."
units.literal: Heilongjiang officers and soldiers each year patrol the mouth of the Ge'erbiji, and every three years also patrol to Xingkanshan and return to report: at year's end report to the ministry."

units.zh: 上從之。
units.en: The emperor approved these proposals.
units.literal: The emperor approved.

units.zh: 富僧阿治事嚴，嘗疏請罪人予官兵為奴，併其妻子皆令為奴；
units.en: Fu Senga ran a tight administration. He once asked that convicted offenders be assigned as bondsmen to troops, together with their wives and children;
units.literal: Fu Senga was strict in administration; he once memorialized requesting that criminals be given to officers and soldiers as slaves, and that their wives and children likewise be made slaves;

units.zh: 又以遣犯脫走，出巡並將校婪索，皆請逮送刑部：上不許。
units.en: and when exiled convicts escaped or officers on tour were caught extorting bribes, he asked that they be sent to the Ministry of Justice for punishment—the emperor declined each request.
units.literal: also because exiled convicts escaped, and on inspection tours commanders and officers extorted greedily, all requested to be arrested and sent to the Ministry of Justice: the emperor did not permit it.

units.zh: 移西安將軍，西安、寧夏移駐滿洲兵，復分駐巴里坤，富僧阿議定規制，皆如所請。
units.en: Transferred to Xi'an as frontier general, he drew up the regulations for redeploying Manchu garrisons from Xi'an and Ningxia and posting detachments at Barkol; the court adopted his plans in full.
units.literal: Transferred to general at Xi'an; Manchu troops relocated from Xi'an and Ningxia, again distributed to garrison at Barkol—Fu Senga's proposed regulations were all granted as requested.

units.zh: 乾隆四十年三月，卒官。
units.en: He died in office in the third month of the fortieth year of the Qianlong reign.
units.literal: In the third month of the fortieth year of Qianlong, he died in office.

units.zh: 伊勒圖，納喇氏，滿洲正白旗人。
units.en: Yi Leitu, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
units.literal: Yi Leitu, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

units.zh: 乾隆初，以世管佐領授三等侍衛，累遷鑲紅旗蒙古副都統。
units.en: Early in the Qianlong reign he entered service as Third Class Bodyguard through his hereditary company captaincy and rose to deputy military governor of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong, by hereditary company captain he was appointed Third Class Bodyguard and was repeatedly promoted to deputy military governor of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.

units.zh: 出駐烏魯木齊，移阿克蘇。
units.en: Posted to the northwest, he garrisoned Urumqi and was later transferred to Aksu.
units.literal: He went out to garrison Urumqi and was transferred to Aksu.

units.zh: 三十二年，授伊犁參贊大臣，移喀什噶爾。
units.en: In the thirty-second year of Qianlong he became assistant military governor at Ili and was moved to Kashgar.
units.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed Ili assistant military governor and transferred to Kashgar.

units.zh: 內擢理籓院尚書，外授伊犁將軍。
units.en: Promoted to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs at court, he was simultaneously appointed Ili general on the frontier.
units.literal: He was promoted within to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and appointed without to Ili general.

units.zh: 三十四年，師徵緬甸，授副將軍，從經略大學士傅恆分道進軍，緬甸人拒戛鳩江，築寨。
units.en: In the thirty-fourth year, during the Burma campaign, he was made deputy commander and marched with Grand Secretary Fu Heng along a separate route; the Burmese held the Jiayu River line behind fortified stockades.
units.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, when the army campaigned against Burma, he was appointed deputy general; following Grand Secretary Fu Heng he advanced by separate routes; the Burmese blocked the Jiayu River and built stockades.

units.zh: 伊勒圖偕參贊大臣阿里袞與戰，奪寨三，殺賊五千餘。
units.en: Yi Leitu fought alongside Assistant Military Governor Aligun, took three stockades, and killed more than five thousand of the enemy.
units.literal: Yi Leitu together with Assistant Military Governor Agui fought, captured three stockades, and killed more than five thousand rebels.

units.zh: 師還，授兵部尚書。
units.en: After the campaign he was appointed minister of war.
units.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed minister of war.

units.zh: 复外授伊犁將軍。
units.en: He was again posted as Ili general on the frontier.
units.literal: Again he was appointed without to Ili general.

units.zh: 土爾扈特汗渥巴錫、台吉策伯克多爾濟等率所部三萬餘戶來歸，先期使至伊犁，具書通款。
units.en: Torghut Khan Ubashi, Taiji Cebeke Duolji, and others led more than thirty thousand households of their people back to allegiance, having sent envoys ahead to Ili with letters of submission.
units.literal: The Torghut khan Oboi, the taiji Cebeke Duolji, and others led more than thirty thousand households of their tribes to submit; beforehand envoys reached Ili with letters expressing goodwill.

units.zh: 伊勒圖以聞，高宗命加意撫綏，俾得所。
units.en: Yi Leitu reported the arrival to the throne, and the Qianlong Emperor ordered that they be settled with particular care.
units.literal: Yi Leitu reported it; the Gaozong emperor ordered special care in pacification so they might find their place.

units.zh: 於是土爾扈特部悉內附，哈薩克、布魯特兩​​部厄魯特降者日眾。
units.en: The Torghuts were thus fully brought within the empire, and Oirats of the Kazakh and Burut tribes came over in growing numbers day by day.
units.literal: Thereupon the entire Torghut tribe submitted within; among the Kazakh and Burut two tribes, Oirat submitters daily grew numerous.

units.zh: 伊勒圖請增置佐領，俾領其眾，從之。
units.en: Yi Leitu asked that additional company captaincies be created to command the new tribesmen, and the court agreed.
units.literal: Yi Leitu requested additional company captains to lead their masses; it was approved.

units.zh: 三十六年，左授參贊大臣，駐烏什，移塔爾巴哈台。
units.en: In the thirty-sixth year he was reassigned as assistant military governor, first at Ushi and then at Tarbagatai.
units.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred left to assistant military governor, garrisoned at Ushi, transferred to Tarbagatai.

units.zh: 三十八年，复授伊犁將軍。
units.en: In the thirty-eighth year he was again made Ili general.
units.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was again appointed Ili general.

units.zh: 兵部議禁鳥槍，伊勒圖以土爾扈特部新歸附，牧馬禦豺虎恃鳥槍，不當一體收禁。
units.en: When the Ministry of War proposed a general ban on firearms, Yi Leitu argued that the newly submitted Torghuts relied on muskets to herd their horses and drive off predators, and should not be disarmed wholesale.
units.literal: The Ministry of War deliberated prohibiting muskets; Yi Leitu argued that the Torghut tribe had newly submitted, herding horses and defending against jackals and tigers relied on muskets, and they should not all be confiscated alike.

units.zh: 四十八年，加太子太保，賜雙眼花翎。
units.en: In the forty-eighth year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
units.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

units.zh: 五十年七月，卒，諡襄武，封一等伯，祀賢良祠。
units.en: He died in the seventh month of the fiftieth year and was posthumously titled Xiangwu, created a first-class baron, and entered for worship in the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the fiftieth year he died; posthumous title Xiangwu, enfeoffed as first-class baron, worshipped in the Temple of Eminent Statesmen.

units.zh: 發帑金千，遣侍衛豐伸濟倫如伊犁賜奠。
units.en: The court issued a thousand taels from the treasury and sent Bodyguard Fengshen Jilun to Ili to offer libations on the emperor's behalf.
units.literal: A thousand taels from the treasury were issued; Bodyguard Fengshen Jilun was dispatched to Ili to confer funeral offerings.

units.zh: 伊勒圖在邊二十餘年，諸所經畫，縝密垂久遠。
units.en: Yi Leitu spent more than twenty years on the frontier, and every policy he devised was careful, thorough, and built to last.
units.literal: Yi Leitu was on the frontier more than twenty years; all he planned was meticulous and enduring for long ages.

units.zh: 其在塔爾巴哈台受代去，上諭繼任參贊大臣慶桂循其規制。
units.en: When he left Tarbagatai upon relief from command, the emperor told his successor Qinggui to adhere to the systems he had established.
units.literal: When he was relieved at Tarbagatai, the emperor instructed his successor Assistant Military Governor Qinggui to follow his regulations.

units.zh: 鎮伊犁尤久，伊犁屯田，請兵得攜妻子。
units.en: His longest tenure was at Ili, where he secured permission for garrison colonists to bring their families.
units.literal: He garrisoned Ili especially long; for Ili military colonies he requested that soldiers be allowed to bring wives and children.

units.zh: 於塔爾奇溝口外烏可爾博蘇克、東察罕烏蘇、霍爾果斯、巴彥岱諸地築城堡，水足地厚，俾得久屯。
units.en: He built fortified settlements beyond Ta'erqi Pass at Wuke'erbosuke, Dongchahanwusu, Huo'erguosi, Bayandai, and other sites where water and soil were good enough to sustain permanent garrisons.
units.literal: Outside the mouth of Ta'erqi Gully at Wuke'erbosuke, Dongchahanwusu, Huo'erguosi, Bayandai, and other places he built fortresses; water was ample and land fertile, enabling long-term garrison farming.

units.zh: 設寶伊局鑄錢，採哈爾哈圖銅礦，三年得九千餘斤，令加鑄，於烏什鑄普爾。
units.en: He founded the Baoyi mint, opened the Kharhatu copper mine—which yielded more than nine thousand jin of ore in three years—and ordered additional coinage, including the casting of pūl at Ushi.
units.literal: He established the Baoyi mint to cast coin; the Kharhatu copper mine was worked, yielding more than nine thousand jin in three years; he ordered increased casting and at Ushi cast pūl.

units.zh: 烏什及庫車、哈喇沙爾諸城與伊犁錢並用，普爾，回錢名也。
units.en: The coins circulated together with Ili currency at Ushi, Kuche, Karashahr, and other towns; pūl was the local name for the Muslim-style cash.
units.literal: Ushi and the cities of Kuche, Karashahr, and others used Ili coin jointly; pūl is the name of Hui money.

units.zh: 又於崆郭羅鄂博諸地採煤，聽商人充窯戶，徵其稅。
units.en: He also opened coal mines around Kongguoluoebo, allowed merchants to operate the kilns, and collected tax on their output.
units.literal: Also at Kongguoluoebo and other places coal was mined; merchants were permitted to serve as kiln masters and taxes were levied on them.

units.zh: 都統海祿請令遣犯皆入鐵廠，與罪人畀官兵為奴者同例。
units.en: Commandant Hailu proposed that all exiled convicts be sent to the ironworks on the same footing as criminals assigned as bondsmen to troops.
units.literal: Commandant Hailu requested that all exiled convicts enter ironworks, on the same precedent as criminals given to officers and soldiers as slaves.

units.zh: 伊勒圖請仍如舊制，使遣犯與為奴者有別。
units.en: Yi Leitu asked that the old distinction be preserved between exiled convicts and convicts formally enslaved to the military.
units.literal: Yi Leitu requested to keep the old system, making exiled convicts distinct from those made slaves.

units.zh: 其卒，上稱其鎮靜妥協，各部落皆心服，封卹特厚。
units.en: At his death the emperor praised his steady, conciliatory rule, noting that every tribe had come to trust him, and granted him unusually lavish posthumous honors.
units.literal: At his death the emperor praised his calm and accommodating manner; all tribes were convinced in heart; enfeoffment and mourning gifts were especially generous.

units.zh: 胡貴，字爾恆，福建同安人。
units.en: Hu Gui, styled Erheng, came from Tong'an in Fujian.
units.literal: Hu Gui, style name Erheng, was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.

units.zh: 少有智略。
units.en: Even as a young man he showed keen judgment and resourcefulness.
units.literal: From youth he had intelligence and stratagem.

units.zh: 入伍，稍遷水師提標右營千總。
units.en: He enlisted and rose in due course to company commander in the Right Battalion of the naval commander's brigade.
units.literal: He entered the army and was gradually promoted to company commander of the Right Battalion of the naval commander's standard.

units.zh: 雍正六年，齎奏入都，世宗召入見。
units.en: In the sixth year of Yongzheng he brought a memorial to the capital and was received in audience by the Yongzheng Emperor.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng he carried a memorial to the capital; the Shizong emperor summoned him for an audience.

units.zh: 再遷後營游擊。
units.en: He was soon promoted to battalion commander of the Rear Battalion.
units.literal: He was again promoted to battalion commander of the Rear Battalion.

units.zh: 監修戰艦，出巡海，坐誤工，吏議當左授，上特宥之。
units.en: While supervising warship repairs and patrolling at sea he was found negligent; the personnel office recommended demotion, but the emperor pardoned him.
units.literal: Supervising repair of warships, on a sea patrol he was charged with delay in work; clerks judged he should be demoted; the emperor specially pardoned him.

units.zh: 累遷江南蘇松鎮總兵。
units.en: He rose in due course to regional commander of the Susong Garrison in Jiangnan.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of the Susong Garrison in Jiangnan.

units.zh: 督運漕糧十萬轉海賑福建，道溫州鳳凰洋，颶作，損米五百餘，請出私財以償。
units.en: Ordered to ship one hundred thousand piculs of grain tribute by sea to relieve famine in Fujian, he was caught in a typhoon off Wenzhou's Fenghuang Sea and lost more than five hundred piculs; he offered to make good the loss from his own purse.
units.literal: Supervising transport of one hundred thousand piculs of grain tribute by sea to relieve Fujian, passing Fenghuang Sea off Wenzhou, a typhoon arose and more than five hundred piculs of grain were lost; he requested to pay compensation from private wealth.

units.zh: 高宗諭曰：「冒險已可嘉，豈有復令出私財償米之理？」
units.en: The Qianlong Emperor replied: "Your willingness to brave the seas is praise enough—how could I ask you to make good the grain from your own funds?"
units.literal: The Gaozong emperor instructed: "Taking risks is already praiseworthy—how could there be reason further to make him pay grain from private wealth?"

units.zh: 命罷勿償。
units.en: He ordered that the offer be declined and the matter closed.
units.literal: He ordered the matter dropped and no compensation.

units.zh: 旋坐廢弛當奪職，复特宥之。
units.en: Shortly afterward he was again found remiss in duty and liable to dismissal, and again the emperor spared him.
units.literal: Soon after, charged with lax administration deserving dismissal from office, he was again specially pardoned.

units.zh: 疏言：「本鎮春、秋兩哨，中營游擊司糧餉，奇兵營游擊職城守，例不出巡。
units.en: He memorialized: "In this command's spring and autumn patrol seasons the Middle Battalion commander handles rations while the Odd Troops Battalion commander holds the city; by custom neither leaves post for sea patrol.
units.literal: He memorialized: "This garrison's spring and autumn patrol seasons—the Middle Battalion battalion commander manages provisions, the Odd Troops Battalion battalion commander's duty is city defense; by precedent they do not go on patrol.

units.zh: 惟既任水師，​​當知海道，應從眾出巡。
units.en: Yet as naval officers they ought to know the sea lanes and should take part in the general patrols.
units.literal: Yet having been assigned to the navy, they ought to know sea routes and should join the general patrol.

units.zh: 陸路將士原改水師者，先令出海演試，如有膽略，量為改補。」
units.en: Soldiers transferred from the army to the navy should first be sent to sea for trial; those who prove steady and bold may be confirmed in naval posts according to merit."
units.literal: Land-force officers and soldiers originally transferred to the navy should first be ordered to go to sea for trial exercises; if they have courage and resource, appoint them to posts as appropriate."

units.zh: 並從所請。
units.en: The court approved every point.
units.literal: All was granted as requested.

units.zh: 崇明海漲，沒民廬。
units.en: A tidal surge at Chongming drowned countless homes.
units.literal: At Chongming the sea surged and submerged commoners' dwellings.

units.zh: 召縣吏議賑，吏言當待請。
units.en: He summoned the county officials to plan relief, but they said they must await imperial authorization.
units.literal: He summoned county clerks to discuss relief; the clerks said they should wait for a request.

units.zh: 貴曰：「民死在頃刻，豈能俟報？
units.en: Hu said: "People are dying this very hour—how can we wait on paperwork?
units.literal: Gui said: "The people die in an instant—how can we wait for a report?

units.zh: 有譴吾任之。」
units.en: If punishment follows, I alone will answer for it."
units.literal: If there is punishment, I will bear it."

units.zh: 即發倉以賑，令所屬為助，眾有難色，貴曰：「設官非以衛民乎？
units.en: He opened the granaries at once and ordered his subordinates to help; when they hesitated he said, "Are we not put in office precisely to protect the people?
units.literal: He immediately opened the granary for relief and ordered subordinates to assist; the crowd showed reluctance; Gui said: "Are offices not established to protect the people?

units.zh: 賑不週，生它變，豈能免患？」
units.en: If relief falls short and unrest follows, who among us will escape blame?"
units.literal: If relief is not thorough, other troubles arise—how can we escape calamity?"

units.zh: 疏請發帑金十八萬、倉穀二十八萬，並留漕米續賑，上深嘉之。
units.en: He then memorialized for 180,000 taels from the treasury, 280,000 piculs from the public granaries, and retention of grain-transport rice for further relief; the emperor commended him warmly.
units.literal: He memorialized requesting disbursement of 180,000 taels from the treasury and 280,000 piculs from the granary, and also retaining grain tribute transport grain for continued relief; the emperor deeply praised it.

units.zh: 歷廣東潮州、瓊州諸鎮，擢提督。
units.en: After serving at the Chaozhou and Qiongzhou garrisons in Guangdong he was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief.
units.literal: He served successively at the garrisons of Chaozhou and Qiongzhou in Guangdong and was promoted to provincial naval commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 增城民王亮臣為亂，貴勒兵馳赴，分遣所屬防隘，扼賊走路。
units.en: When Wang Liangchen of Zengcheng rose in revolt, Hu led his troops posthaste, posted detachments at the passes, and cut off the rebels' lines of retreat.
units.literal: The commoner Wang Liangchen of Zengcheng raised a rebellion; Gui urged troops to rush there, dispatched subordinates to guard passes, and blocked the rebels' escape routes.

units.zh: 總督阿里袞軍亦至，分道捕治，諸賊皆就擒。
units.en: Governor-General Aligun's force arrived as well; operating on separate lines they rounded up the rebels until every band was taken.
units.literal: Governor-General Agui's army also arrived; by separate routes they pursued and suppressed, and all rebels were captured.

units.zh: 以失察自劾，貸勿問，仍敘勞。
units.en: He impeached himself for having failed to detect the plot in time; the court waived punishment and still recorded his merit.
units.literal: For failure of oversight he impeached himself; he was pardoned without inquiry and still given merit recognition.

units.zh: 入覲，賜花翎。
units.en: At court audience he was granted the peacock feather.
units.literal: On entering audience he was awarded the peacock feather.

units.zh: 移福建水師提督，復自浙江還廣東。
units.en: He was transferred to command the Fujian naval forces, then returned to Guangdong by way of Zhejiang.
units.literal: Transferred to Fujian naval commander-in-chief, again from Zhejiang back to Guangdong.

units.zh: 乾隆二十五年，卒，諡勤愨。
units.en: He died in the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong and was posthumously titled Qinque.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong he died; posthumous title Qinmin.

units.zh: 子振聲，附李長庚傳。
units.en: His son Zhensheng is treated in the biography of Li Changgeng.
units.literal: His son Zhensheng is appended to the biography of Li Changgeng.

units.zh: 俞金鼇，字厚菴，直隸天津人。
units.en: Yu Jin'ao, styled Hou'an, came from Tianjin in Zhili.
units.literal: Yu Jin'ao, style name Hou'an, was a native of Tianjin in Zhili.

units.zh: 乾隆七年武進士，授藍翎侍衛。
units.en: A military jinshi of the seventh year of Qianlong, he was appointed a Blue Feather Bodyguard.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong he passed the military jinshi examination and was appointed a Blue Feather Bodyguard.

units.zh: 以守備發山東，累遷甘肅肅州鎮總兵。
units.en: Posted to Shandong as garrison commander, he rose in due course to regional commander of the Suzhou Garrison in Gansu.
units.literal: As garrison commander he was dispatched to Shandong and was repeatedly promoted to regional commander of the Suzhou Garrison in Gansu.

units.zh: 命如伊犁董理屯田，歲豐，伊犁將軍伊勒圖奏綠營兵二千二百名，人穫米二十八石有奇。
units.en: Sent to Ili to oversee military farming, he brought in a bumper harvest; Ili General Yi Leitu reported that his 2,200 Green Standard troops averaged more than twenty-eight piculs of grain per man.
units.literal: Ordered to proceed to Ili to supervise military colonies; the year was abundant; Ili General Yi Leitu memorialized that among 2,200 Green Standard soldiers, each man harvested a little more than twenty-eight piculs of grain.

units.zh: 得旨，敘勞。
units.en: An imperial rescript followed, recording his merit.
units.literal: He received the imperial rescript and was given merit recognition.

units.zh: 移巴里坤總兵，擢烏魯木齊提督，仍領屯田事。
units.en: Transferred to Barkol as regional commander and promoted to provincial commander-in-chief at Urumqi, he continued to direct the colony farms.
units.literal: Transferred to regional commander at Barkol, promoted to provincial commander-in-chief at Urumqi, still overseeing military colony affairs.

units.zh: 奏請移沙州副將駐安西，巴里坤迤西至瑪納斯，擇有水草地設墩塘，皆議行。
units.en: He asked that the Shazhou brigade deputy be moved to Anxi and that beacon towers and posts be placed at watered sites from Barkol west to Manas; the court approved each proposal.
units.literal: He memorialized requesting transfer of the Shazhou brigade deputy to garrison Anxi; from Barkol westward to Manas, selecting places with water and pasture to set beacon towers and posts—all were deliberated and implemented.

units.zh: 時令移軍戍烏魯木齊及瑪納斯，得挈妻子以往，謂之「眷兵」。
units.en: Troops then being shifted to garrison Urumqi and Manas were allowed to bring their families; such settlers were called "family troops."
units.literal: At that time troops were ordered transferred to garrison Urumqi and Manas, permitted to bring wives and children—called "family troops."

units.zh: 金鼇請具一歲糧，亦從其請。
units.en: Jin'ao asked that a full year's rations be issued in advance, and that request too was granted.
units.literal: Jin'ao requested provision of one year's grain; that too was granted.

units.zh: 歷江南、福建、甘肅諸省提督。
units.en: He later held the post of provincial commander-in-chief in Jiangnan, Fujian, Gansu, and other provinces in turn.
units.literal: He served successively as provincial commander-in-chief in Jiangnan, Fujian, Gansu, and other provinces.

units.zh: 固原回李化玉與河州回田五糾眾為亂，攻靖遠，金鼇與涼州副都統圖桑阿合軍討之，逐賊馬營街，固原提督剛塔亦以師來會，多所斬獲。
units.en: When the Guyuan Muslim Li Huayu and the Hezhou Muslim Tian Wu raised followers and attacked Jingyuan, Jin'ao joined Deputy Military Governor Tusang'a of Liangzhou to suppress them, driving the rebels toward Maying Street; Guyuan Commander-in-Chief Gangta brought his force to the rendezvous as well, and together they killed or captured a great number of the enemy.
units.literal: The Hui of Guyuan, Li Huayu, and the Hui of Hezhou, Tian Wu, gathered crowds in rebellion and attacked Jingyuan; Jin'ao together with Deputy Military Governor Tusang'a of Liangzhou combined armies to suppress them, driving the rebels to Maying Street; Guyuan Commander-in-Chief Gangta also brought troops to join, and many were beheaded or captured.

units.zh: 土司楊宗業以土兵助戰，賊憑山設拒，土兵敗走，金鼇擊賊退。
units.en: The tusi Yang Zongye sent native levies to help, but the rebels held the heights and routed the auxiliaries; Jin'ao then struck and forced the rebels to withdraw.
units.literal: Tusi Yang Zongye aided the fight with native troops; the rebels relied on the mountains to set defenses; the native troops were defeated and fled; Jin'ao attacked and drove the rebels back.

units.zh: 賊夜走石峰堡，糾會寧諸回，勢复張，副都統明善戰死。
units.en: The rebels slipped away by night to Shifeng Fort, rallied the Muslims of Huining, and grew bold again; Deputy Military Governor Mingshan fell in battle.
units.literal: The rebels fled by night to Shifeng Fort, rallied the Hui of Huining, and their power revived; Deputy Military Governor Mingshan died in battle.

units.zh: 金鼇進次烏家坪，擊賊，斃頭人三，擒二十有九。
units.en: Jin'ao advanced to Wujiaping, engaged the rebels, killed three of their leaders, and took twenty-nine prisoners.
units.literal: Jin'ao advanced and encamped at Wujiaping, attacked the rebels, killed three ringleaders, and captured twenty-nine.

units.zh: 轉戰至秦安土鼓山，賊敗竄蓮花城，師從之，至於雙峴，從總督李侍堯自中路進攻，敗之。
units.en: Fighting on to Tugu Mountain in Qin'an, he routed the rebels when they bolted for Lianhua City; the army pursued to Shuangxian, and in concert with Governor-General Li Shiyao's central column he defeated them again.
units.literal: Turning to fight at Tugu Mountain in Qin'an, the rebels were defeated and fled to Lianhua City; the army followed to Shuangxian; following Governor-General Li Shiyao's central-route attack, they were defeated.

units.zh: 福康安督兵剿石峰堡，令金鼇防底店護運道。
units.en: When Fuk'anggan took command against Shifeng Fort, he stationed Jin'ao at Didian to secure the supply line.
units.literal: Fuk'anggan supervised troops to suppress Shifeng Fort and ordered Jin'ao to guard Didian and protect the transport route.

units.zh: 回亂定，移湖廣。
units.en: After the Muslim uprising was pacified he was transferred to Huguang.
units.literal: When the Hui rebellion was settled, he was transferred to Huguang.

units.zh: 复移直隸，未行，鳳凰廳苗石滿宜糾眾為亂，金鼇聞報馳赴，令鎮筸鎮總兵尹德禧督軍破賊寨，生致其渠。
units.en: He was reassigned to Zhili but had not yet left when the Miao leader Shi Manyi of Fenghuang raised a revolt; Jin'ao hurried to the scene and ordered Zhen'ao Garrison Commander Yin Dexi to storm the rebel stockade and take the chief alive.
units.literal: Again transferred to Zhili; before departing, the Miao Shi Manyi of Fenghuang ting gathered crowds in rebellion; Jin'ao on hearing the report rushed there and ordered Zhen'ao Garrison Regional Commander Yin Dexi to supervise troops in breaking the rebel stockade and capturing the ringleader alive.

units.zh: 上以金鼇習苗疆事，命仍留湖廣。
units.en: Because Jin'ao was experienced in Miao frontier affairs, the emperor ordered him to remain in Huguang.
units.literal: The emperor, because Jin'ao was versed in Miao frontier affairs, ordered him to remain in Huguang.

units.zh: 台灣林爽文為亂，命德禧將湖北兵二千以往，金鼇出駐鳳凰廳鎮苗疆。
units.en: When Lin Shuangwen rose in Taiwan, Yin Dexi was sent with two thousand Hubei troops while Jin'ao remained to garrison Fenghuang and keep the Miao frontier quiet.
units.literal: Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan; Dexi was ordered to lead two thousand Hubei troops there; Jin'ao went out to garrison Fenghuang ting and pacify the Miao frontier.

units.zh: 旋入覲，命在乾清門行走，賜紫禁城騎馬。
units.en: He soon came to court, was assigned duty at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and was granted the privilege of riding inside the Forbidden City.
units.literal: Soon after he entered audience and was ordered to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity; he was granted riding within the Forbidden City.

units.zh: 引疾乞罷，上以金鼇有勞，下總督畢沅察病狀，乃加左都督，允解官歸。
units.en: He pleaded illness and asked to retire; the emperor, mindful of his service, had Governor-General Bi Yuan verify his condition, promoted him to Left Commissioner-in-Chief, and allowed him to resign and return home.
units.literal: Citing illness he requested retirement; the emperor, because Jin'ao had merit, sent orders to Governor-General Bi Yuan to examine his condition; then he was given the additional rank of Left Commissioner-in-Chief and permitted to resign and return home.

units.zh: 旋卒。
units.en: He died shortly afterward.
units.literal: Soon after he died.

units.zh: 金鼇嘗預千叟宴，高宗賜之酒，命賦詩記事，金鼇辭不能詩。
units.en: Jin'ao once attended the Banquet for a Thousand Elders; the Qianlong Emperor offered him wine and asked him to compose a commemorative poem, but Jin'ao begged off, saying he was no poet.
units.literal: Jin'ao once attended the Banquet for a Thousand Elders; the Gaozong emperor bestowed wine on him and ordered him to compose a poem recording the event; Jin'ao declined, saying he could not write poetry.

units.zh: 上顧笑曰：「汝為香樹妻弟，又從受業，豈不能詩者？」
units.en: The emperor turned with a smile and said, "You are the brother-in-law of Xiangshu and studied under him as well—how can you claim you cannot write verse?"
units.literal: The emperor looked back smiling and said: "You are the wife's younger brother of Xiangshu and also studied under him—how could you be unable to write poetry?"

units.zh: 香樹，錢陳群字也。
units.en: Xiangshu was the style name of the scholar Qian Chenqun.
units.literal: Xiangshu was the style name of Qian Chenqun.

units.zh: 官湖廣，和珅已柄政，欲納交焉。
units.en: While serving in Huguang, when Heshen already dominated the government, Heshen sought his friendship.
units.literal: When he held office in Huguang, Heshen already wielded power and wished to win his friendship.

units.zh: 金鼇謝不可。
units.en: Jin'ao politely refused.
units.literal: Jin'ao declined and would not agree.

units.zh: 尹德禧，鑲黃旗包衣人，初名色喀通額。
units.en: Yin Dexi was originally a bondservant of the Bordered Yellow Banner named Seketong'e.
units.literal: Yin Dexi was a bondservant of the Bordered Yellow Banner; his original name was Seketong'e.

units.zh: 以領催從征伊犁，遷至防禦。
units.en: Serving as a company clerk on the Ili campaign, he rose to garrison defense commandant.
units.literal: As a company clerk he followed the campaign to Ili and was promoted to garrison defense commandant.

units.zh: 開戶出旗，更姓名，改籍直隸密雲縣。
units.en: He established an independent household, left the banner rolls, took a new name, and registered as a native of Miyun County in Zhili.
units.literal: He opened a household and left the banner, changed his name, and altered his register to Miyun County in Zhili.

units.zh: 從征金川，复六遷至總兵。
units.en: On the Jinchuan campaign he was promoted six more times until he became a regional commander.
units.literal: He followed the Jinchuan campaign and after six more promotions reached regional commander.

units.zh: 石滿宜據句捕砦為亂，德禧破砦獲滿宜，賜花翎。
units.en: When Shi Manyi seized Jubu stockade in revolt, Dexi stormed the fort, captured him, and was granted the peacock feather.
units.literal: Shi Manyi held Jubu stockade in rebellion; Dexi broke the stockade and captured Manyi, and was awarded the peacock feather.

units.zh: 上詰德禧：「當苗亂，何不專摺奏？」
units.en: The emperor rebuked him: "During the Miao uprising, why did you not report directly by memorial?"
units.literal: The emperor interrogated Dexi: "When the Miao rebelled, why did you not submit a separate memorial?"

units.zh: 德禧請罪，命貸之。
units.en: He pleaded guilty and was pardoned.
units.literal: Dexi pleaded guilty and was ordered pardoned.

units.zh: 搜捕滿宜餘黨，苗疆悉定。
units.en: After hunting down Manyi's remaining followers the Miao frontier was fully pacified.
units.literal: Searching out Manyi's remaining followers, the Miao frontier was entirely settled.

units.zh: 其出師台灣，師至，爽文已就俘，福康安令德禧屯竹仔港防賊逸。
units.en: On the Taiwan expedition the army arrived only after Shuangwen had been taken; Fuk'anggan stationed Dexi at Zhuzai Harbor to block any rebel escape by sea.
units.literal: When he marched to Taiwan, the army arrived after Shuangwen had already been captured; Fuk'anggan ordered Dexi to encamp at Zhuzai Harbor to prevent rebels escaping.

units.zh: 台灣定，召入見，令署湖南提督。
units.en: After Taiwan was pacified he was called to court and appointed acting provincial commander-in-chief of Hunan.
units.literal: When Taiwan was settled he was summoned to audience and ordered to act as Hunan provincial commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 卒，遺言請還旗籍，复隸鑲黃旗包衣。
units.en: At his death he asked in his final wishes to be restored to the banner registers as a bondservant of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
units.literal: He died; his final request was to return to banner register, again subordinated to the Bordered Yellow Banner bondservant rolls.

units.zh: 剛塔，烏濟克忒氏，滿洲正藍旗人。
units.en: Gangta, of the Ujikete clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Blue Banner.
units.literal: Gangta, of the Ujikete clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

units.zh: 初充前鋒，從征準噶爾，授雲騎尉世職。
units.en: He began as a vanguard on the Dzungar campaigns and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
units.literal: At first he served as a vanguard, followed the campaign against the Dzungars, and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

units.zh: 三遷直隸泰宁鎮中營游擊。
units.en: After three promotions he became battalion commander of the Middle Battalion at the Taining Garrison in Zhili.
units.literal: After three promotions he became battalion commander of the Middle Battalion of the Taining Garrison in Zhili.

units.zh: 從克臨清，山東巡撫楊景素奏留山東。
units.en: He took part in the capture of Linqing, and Shandong Governor Yang Jingsu asked that he be kept in Shandong.
units.literal: He followed in the capture of Linqing; Shandong Governor Yang Jingsu memorialized to retain him in Shandong.

units.zh: 四遷直隸提督，兼領馬蘭鎮總兵。
units.en: Four further promotions brought him to provincial commander-in-chief of Zhili, while he also commanded the Malan Garrison.
units.literal: After four more promotions he became Zhili commander-in-chief, concurrently holding regional command of the Malan Garrison.

units.zh: 移陝西固原提督。
units.en: He was transferred to command the Guyuan garrison in Shaanxi.
units.literal: Transferred to Shaanxi Guyuan commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 乾隆四十九年，鹽茶廳小山回田五糾眾為亂，攻破安西州。
units.en: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong the Xiaoshan Muslim Tian Wu of Yancha ting raised followers, rebelled, and overran Anxi Prefecture.
units.literal: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong, the Xiaoshan Hui Tian Wu of Yancha ting gathered crowds in rebellion and stormed Anxi Prefecture.

units.zh: 剛塔督兵逐賊，殺賊數十，射殪乘馬賊渠，賜上用玉韘、大小荷包。
units.en: Gangta led the pursuit, killed dozens of rebels, and shot down the mounted rebel chief; the emperor rewarded him with an imperial jade thumb-ring and large and small purses.
units.literal: Gangta supervised troops pursuing the rebels, killed several tens of rebels, shot dead the mounted rebel chieftain, and was awarded the emperor's jade thumb-ring and large and small purses.

units.zh: 复逐賊至浪山，田五戰被創，自殺。
units.en: Pressing on to Lang Mountain, he wounded Tian Wu in battle; Tian Wu then took his own life.
units.literal: Again pursuing the rebels to Lang Mountain, Tian Wu was wounded in battle and killed himself.

units.zh: 其徒竄據馬家堡，剛塔督兵合圍，賊夜出堡逾山遁，環壘樹木桿，懸衣帽其上，紿官軍，官軍逼壘，乃知賊已走。
units.en: The survivors seized Majia Fort; Gangta invested it, but the rebels slipped out by night over the hills, left poles and clothing on the walls to deceive the besiegers, and were long gone before the troops discovered the ruse.
units.literal: His followers fled and seized Majia Fort; Gangta supervised troops in combined encirclement; the rebels by night left the fort and escaped over the mountains; they ringed the ramparts with wooden poles and hung clothes and hats on them to deceive the government army; when the government army pressed the ramparts, only then did they know the rebels had already fled.

units.zh: 剛塔督兵逐賊，戰於馬家灣，剛塔中矢。
units.en: Gangta continued the pursuit and fought at Majia Bay, where he was wounded by an arrow.
units.literal: Gangta supervised troops pursuing the rebels, fought at Majia Bay, and Gangta was struck by an arrow.

units.zh: 復進至馬營街，殺賊數十，得級二十五。
units.en: Advancing again to Maying Street, he killed dozens of rebels and took twenty-five heads.
units.literal: Advancing again to Maying Street, he killed several tens of rebels and obtained twenty-five heads.

units.zh: 賊攻陷通渭，其徒分據石峰堡。
units.en: The rebels then overran Tongwei while their bands occupied Shifeng Fort.
units.literal: The rebels stormed and took Tongwei; their followers separately held Shifeng Fort.

units.zh: 西安副都統明善攻之，沒於陣。
units.en: Xi'an Deputy Military Governor Mingshan assaulted the fort and was killed in action.
units.literal: Xi'an Deputy Military Governor Mingshan attacked it and perished in battle.

units.zh: 上以師無功，令大學士阿桂、尚書福康安出視師。
units.en: Because the campaign stalled, the emperor sent Grand Secretary Agui and Minister Fuk'anggan to take command in the field.
units.literal: The emperor, because the army had no success, ordered Grand Secretary Agui and Minister Fuk'anggan to go out and inspect the army.

units.zh: 上謂馬營街、石峰堡皆通渭地，剛塔方逐賊馬營街，通渭陷不赴援，明善又以攻石峰堡戰死，詔詰責。
units.en: The emperor observed that Maying Street and Shifeng Fort lay within Tongwei: Gangta had been chasing rebels at Maying Street when Tongwei fell yet he did not march to its relief, and Mingshan had died assaulting Shifeng Fort—an edict censured him sharply.
units.literal: The emperor said Maying Street and Shifeng Fort are both in Tongwei territory; Gangta was just pursuing rebels at Maying Street when Tongwei fell and he did not go to relieve it; Mingshan also died attacking Shifeng Fort; an edict rebuked and held him accountable.

units.zh: 剛塔疏言：「獲賊言將自通渭道伏羌、秦州天潼關。」
units.en: Gangta memorialized, "Prisoners said the rebels would march from Tongwei through Fuxiang and Qinzhou toward Tiantong Pass."
units.literal: Gangta memorialized: "Capturing rebels, they said they would go from Tongwei by way of Fuxiang and Qinzhou to Tiantong Pass."

units.zh: 上責剛塔信賊妄語搖軍心，令福康安傳諭，奪剛塔職，逮送京師。
units.en: The emperor accused him of crediting rebel bluster and unsettling the troops, had Fuk'anggan relay the edict, stripped him of rank, and sent him under arrest to the capital.
units.literal: The emperor rebuked Gangta for believing the rebels' false words and shaking army morale, ordered Fuk'anggan to transmit the edict, stripped Gangta of office, and had him arrested and sent to the capital.

units.zh: 上方幸熱河，留京王大臣等讞當斬，上以剛塔殲賊渠田五，戰馬家灣身被創，貸死，戍伊犁。
units.en: The emperor was at Rehe; the princes and ministers in Beijing recommended execution, but noting that Gangta had destroyed the rebel chief Tian Wu and been wounded at Majia Bay, the emperor spared his life and banished him to Ili.
units.literal: The emperor was then visiting Rehe; the princes and grand ministers left in the capital judged death by decapitation; the emperor, because Gangta had destroyed the rebel chieftain Tian Wu and at Majia Bay was wounded in battle, commuted death and exiled him to garrison duty at Ili.

units.zh: 卒。
units.en: He died there in exile.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 論曰：富僧阿鎮黑龍江，察國界，定巡徼之制。
units.en: The historians remark: Fu Senga, as commander at Heilongjiang, surveyed the national boundary and instituted a lasting system of frontier patrols.
units.literal: The commentary says: Fu Senga garrisoned Heilongjiang, inspected the national boundary, and established the patrol system.

units.zh: 伊勒圖鎮伊犁，徠屬部，著拊循之績。
units.en: Yi Leitu, holding Ili, brought dependent tribes within the fold and left a record of wise pastoral governance.
units.literal: Yi Leitu garrisoned Ili, drew subordinate tribes, and showed achievements in comforting and guiding them.

units.zh: 建威銷萌，邊帥之職舉矣。
units.en: By building authority and quelling trouble in its infancy, they fulfilled what frontier commanders are meant to do.
units.literal: Establishing authority and extinguishing troubles at the sprout—the duties of frontier commanders were fully fulfilled.

units.zh: 貴定增城，金鼇、剛塔攻石峰堡，名位顯晦殊，要不可謂無功也，故類次焉。
units.en: Hu Gui pacified Zengcheng; Yu Jin'ao and Gangta fought at Shifeng Fort—their reputations rose and fell in different measure, yet none was without real service; hence they are recorded together in this chapter.
units.literal: Gui pacified Zengcheng; Jin'ao and Gangta attacked Shifeng Fort; fame and position varied between glory and obscurity, but in essentials they cannot be said to have been without merit; therefore they are grouped together in sequence.

units.zh: 五十二年，台灣林爽文為亂，承恩請往討之，師無功，逮詣京師，罪當死，上寬之。
units.en: In year fifty-two, when Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan, Chengen volunteered to suppress him; the campaign failed, he was brought to the capital under arrest, and though his crime warranted death the emperor spared him.
units.literal: In the fifty-second year, Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan; Chengen requested to go suppress him; the army achieved nothing, he was arrested and brought to the capital, his offense merited death, but the emperor showed leniency.

units.zh: 厥後定邊將軍兆惠等、定西將軍阿桂等奏凱，高宗均駐蹕黃新莊行宮，築台郊勞，百官咸會。
units.en: Thereafter when Pacification-of-the-Frontier General Zhao Hui and others and Pacification-of-the-West General Agui and others reported victory, the Gaozong each time halted at the Huangxinzhuang traveling palace, built a platform for suburban welcome, and all officials assembled.
units.literal: Thereafter when Pacification-of-the-Frontier General Zhao Hui and others and Pacification-of-the-West General Agui and others reported victory, the Gaozong each time halted at the Huangxinzhuang traveling palace, built a platform for suburban welcome, and all officials assembled.

units.zh: 將軍暨從征大臣、將士皆擐甲胄，跪紅柱外俟駕。
units.en: The general and the expedition ministers and soldiers all donned armor and knelt outside the red posts awaiting the imperial arrival.
units.literal: The general and expedition ministers and soldiers all donned armor and knelt outside the red posts awaiting the imperial arrival.

units.zh: 帝就拜位立，將軍暨群臣班分東西，鴻臚官贊「跪」，則皆跪。
units.en: The emperor took his position at the kneeling place and stood; the general and officials were arranged in ranks east and west; when the Director of Ceremonies intoned "Kneel," all knelt.
units.literal: The emperor took his position at the kneeling place and stood; the general and officials were arranged in ranks east and west; when the Director of Ceremonies intoned "Kneel," all knelt.

units.zh: 帝拜天，三跪九叩，將軍等如之。
units.en: The emperor bowed to Heaven with three kneelings and nine prostrations, and the generals and others did likewise.
units.literal: The emperor bowed to Heaven with three kneelings and nine prostrations, and the generals and others did likewise.

units.zh: 定金川五十人：將軍阿桂，副將軍豐升額、明亮，大學士舒赫德、於敏中，尚書福隆安，參贊大臣親王色布騰巴爾珠爾，都統海蘭察，護軍統領額森特、舒常，領隊大臣都統奎林、和隆武、福康安，副都統普爾普，荊州將軍興兆，參贊大臣提督哈國興，領隊大臣提督馬彪、馬全、書麟，副都統三保、烏什哈達、瑚尼爾圖、珠爾格德、阿爾都、阿爾薩朗、舒亮、科瑪、伊蘭保、佛倫泰、富興、德赫布、莽喀察，總兵海祿、敖成、官達色​​、成德、欽保、曹順、保寧、特成額、烏爾納，總兵敦柱，侍衛額爾特、托爾托保、泰斐英阿、柏凌、達蘭泰、薩爾吉岱，佐領特爾惇澈，副將興奎。
units.en: For the pacification of Jinchuan, the fifty men honored were: General A Gui; Deputy Generals Fengsheng'e and Mingliang; Grand Secretaries Shuhede and Yu Minzhong; Minister Fulong'an; Assisting Commander Prince Sebeteng Baljur; Commander-in-Chief Hailancha; Guard Commanders Esente and Shuchang; Column Commanders Kuilin, Helongwu, and Fuk'anggan; Vice Commander-in-Chief Pu'erpu; Jingzhou General Xingzhao; Assisting Commander and Regional Commander Ha Guoxing; Column Commanders and Regional Commanders Ma Biao, Ma Quan, and Shu Lin; Vice Commanders Sanbao, Wushi Hada, Huni'ertu, Zhu'ergede, A'erdu, A'ersalang, Shuliang, Kema, Yilanbao, Foluntai, Fuxing, Dehebu, and Mangkacha; Regional Commanders Hailu, Aocheng, Guandase, Chengde, Qinbao, Caoshun, Baoning, Techeng'e, and Wu'erna; Regional Commander Dunzhu; Guards E'erte, Tuo'ertuobao, Taifeiying'a, Boling, Dalantai, and Sa'erjidai; Adjutant Te'erdun Che; and Vice General Xingkui.
units.literal: For the pacification of Jinchuan, fifty men: General A Gui; Deputy Generals Fengsheng'e and Mingliang; Grand Secretaries Shuhede and Yu Minzhong; Minister Fulong'an; Assisting Commander Prince Sebeteng Baljur; Commander-in-Chief Hailancha; Guard Commanders Esente and Shuchang; Column Commanders Kuilin, Helongwu, and Fuk'anggan; Vice Commander-in-Chief Pu'erpu; Jingzhou General Xingzhao; Assisting Commander and Regional Commander Ha Guoxing; Column Commanders and Regional Commanders Ma Biao, Ma Quan, and Shu Lin; Vice Commanders Sanbao, Wushi Hada, Huni'ertu, Zhu'ergede, A'erdu, A'ersalang, Shuliang, Kema, Yilanbao, Foluntai, Fuxing, Dehebu, Mangkacha; Regional Commanders Hailu, Aocheng, Guandase, Chengde, Qinbao, Caoshun, Baoning, Techeng'e, and Wu'erna; Regional Commander Dunzhu; and the guards E'erte, Tuo'ertuobao, Taifeiying'a, Boling, Dalantai, Sa'erjidai, the adjutant Te'erdun Che, and Vice General Xingkui.

units.zh: 四年，高宗崩，大學士和珅得罪，仁宗以福長安阿附，逮下獄，奪爵，籍其家。
units.en: In 1799, after Qianlong's death, Heshen fell; Jiaqing arrested Fuchang'an for siding with Heshen, stripped his rank, and seized his property.
units.literal: In the fourth year, when the Gaozong Emperor died, Grand Secretary Heshen was condemned; the Renzong Emperor, holding that Fuchang'an had fawned on Heshen, had him arrested, stripped of rank, and his property confiscated.

units.zh: 諸大臣議用朋黨律坐立斬，上命改監候，而賜和珅死，使監福長安詣和珅死所跪視。
units.en: Ministers proposed decapitation under the faction law; the emperor commuted it to imprisonment, executed Heshen, and made Fuchang'an watch.
units.literal: The ministers proposed sentencing by the statute on faction, which meant immediate decapitation; the emperor ordered imprisonment awaiting execution instead, and while granting Heshen death ordered Fuchang'an brought to kneel where Heshen died and watch.

units.zh: 定台灣二十人：大學士阿桂、和珅、王杰，協辦大學士福康安，領侍衛內大臣海蘭察，尚書福長安、董誥，總督李侍堯、孫士毅，巡撫徐嗣曾，成都將軍鄂輝，護軍統領舒亮、普爾普，提督蔡攀龍、梁朝柱、許世亨，總兵穆克登阿、張芝元、普吉保，散秩大臣穆塔爾。
units.en: For the pacification of Taiwan, twenty men were honored: Grand Secretaries A Gui, Heshen, and Wang Jie; Associate Grand Secretary Fuk'anggan; Inner Court Minister Hailancha; Ministers Fuchang'an and Dong Gao; Governors-General Li Shiyao and Sun Shiyi; Governor Xu Siceng; Chengdu General E Hui; guard commanders Shuliang and Pu'erpu; regional commanders Cai Panlong, Liang Chaozhu, Xu Shiheng, Mukedeng'a, Zhang Zhiyuan, and Pujibao; and Minister without Portfolio Mutar.
units.literal: For the pacification of Taiwan, twenty men: Grand Secretaries A Gui, Heshen, and Wang Jie; Associate Grand Secretary Fuk'anggan; Inner Court Minister of the Imperial Guard Hailancha; Ministers Fuchang'an and Dong Gao; Governors-General Li Shiyao and Sun Shiyi; Governor Xu Siceng; Chengdu General E Hui; Guard Commanders Shuliang and Pu'erpu; Regional Commanders Cai Panlong, Liang Chaozhu, and Xu Shiheng; Regional Commanders Mukedeng'a, Zhang Zhiyuan, and Pujibao; Minister without Portfolio Mutar.

units.zh: 李長庚子廷鈺胡振聲王得祿邱良功陳步雲
units.en: Li Changgeng, with his son Ting Yu, Hu Zhensheng, Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, and Chen Buyun
units.literal: Li Changgeng, his son Ting Yu, Hu Zhensheng, Wang Delu, Qiu Lianggong, Chen Buyun

units.zh: 李長庚，字西岩，福建同安人。
units.en: Li Changgeng, whose style name was Xiyan, came from Tong'an in Fujian.
units.literal: Li Changgeng, styled Xiyan, was a man of Tong'an in Fujian.

units.zh: 五十九年，夷艇始犯福建三澎，長庚擊走之。
units.en: In the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong, foreign pirate vessels first raided the three Penghu stations off Fujian, and Changgeng beat them back.
units.literal: In the fifty-ninth year foreign pirate junks first attacked the three Penghu islands of Fujian; Changgeng drove them off.

units.zh: 乾隆三十六年武進士，授藍翎侍衛。
units.en: He earned his military jinshi degree in the thirty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign and was appointed a Blue Braid Imperial Guardsman.
units.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he passed the military jinshi examination and was appointed a Blue Braid Guard.

units.zh: 出為浙江衢州營都司，累遷樂清協副將。
units.en: He left the capital to serve as battalion commander of the Quzhou Garrison in Zhejiang, and rose in due course to deputy commander of the Yueqing Brigade.
units.literal: He went out to serve as battalion commander of the Quzhou Garrison in Zhejiang, and was promoted in succession to deputy commander of the Yueqing Brigade.

units.zh: 是年，擢福建水師提督，尋調浙江。
units.en: That year he was made Fujian naval commander-in-chief and was soon transferred to Zhejiang.
units.literal: That year he was promoted to Fujian naval commander-in-chief, and soon was transferred to Zhejiang.

units.zh: 巡撫阮元奏以長庚總統三鎮水師擊之，會師海門。
units.en: Governor Ruan Yuan recommended that Changgeng take overall command of the naval forces of the three garrisons to strike them, and the fleets assembled at Haimen.
units.literal: Governor Ruan Yuan memorialized that Changgeng should command the fleets of the three garrisons to attack them, and the forces united at Haimen.

units.zh: 五十二年，署福建海壇鎮總兵。
units.en: In the fifty-second year of Qianlong he served as acting regional commander of the Haitan garrison in Fujian.
units.literal: In the fifty-second year he acted as regional commander of Haitan Town in Fujian.

units.zh: 鄰海有盜，誤指所轄界，坐褫職。
units.en: When pirates struck waters near his command, he was wrongly blamed for an incident within his jurisdiction and was stripped of his post.
units.literal: Pirates appeared in a neighboring sea area and he was wrongly charged with responsibility for his jurisdiction; he was dismissed from office.

units.zh: 罄家財募鄉勇，捕獲巨盜，起用，補海壇游擊，遷銅山參將。
units.en: He spent his entire family fortune to raise local militia, captured a major pirate leader, was reinstated in service, filled the post of naval lieutenant-colonel at Haitan, and was later promoted to garrison colonel at Tongshan.
units.literal: He exhausted his family wealth to raise local militia, captured a major pirate, was reinstated, was appointed Haitan naval lieutenant-colonel, and was transferred to be garrison colonel at Tongshan.

units.zh: 嘉慶二年，遷澎湖協副將，擢浙江定海鎮總兵。
units.en: In the second year of Jiaqing he became deputy commander of the Penghu Brigade and was then promoted to regional commander of the Dinghai garrison in Zhejiang.
units.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he was transferred to deputy commander of the Penghu Brigade and was promoted to regional commander of Dinghai Town in Zhejiang.

units.zh: 三年，迭擊洋匪於衢港及普陀。
units.en: In the third year he fought sea bandits again and again at Qu Port and Mount Putuo.
units.literal: In the third year he repeatedly attacked sea bandits at Qu Port and Putuo.

units.zh: 四年，鳳尾幫引夷艇入溫州洋，敗之，賜花翎。
units.en: In the fourth year the Fengwei gang guided foreign pirate junks into Wenzhou waters; he routed them and was awarded the peacock feather.
units.literal: In the fourth year the Fengwei gang led foreign junks into the Wenzhou sea; he defeated them and was granted the peacock feather.

units.zh: 五年夏，夷艇合水澳、鳳尾百餘艘萃於浙洋，逼台州。
units.en: That summer in the fifth year, over a hundred foreign pirate craft together with the Shui'ao and Fengwei gangs massed in Zhejiang waters and threatened Taizhou.
units.literal: In the summer of the fifth year, more than a hundred foreign junks together with the Shui'ao and Fengwei gangs gathered in Zhejiang waters and pressed on Taizhou.

units.zh: 賊泊松門山下相持，颶風大作，覆溺幾盡，其泊岸及附敗舟者皆就俘，獲安南偽侯倫貴利等四總兵，磔之，以敕印擲還其國。
units.en: The pirates lay at anchor below Songmen Mountain in a stalemate until a violent typhoon struck and nearly all were sunk; those who reached shore or clung to broken hulls were taken captive. Four Annamese pretender-marquises, including Lun Guili, were captured, executed by dismemberment, and their imperial seals were sent back to their country.
units.literal: The bandits anchored below Songmen Mountain and stood off; a great typhoon arose and nearly all were capsized and drowned; those who reached shore or clung to wrecked boats were all taken prisoner; four Annamese false marquises including Lun Guili were captured, dismembered, and their imperial seals were thrown back to their country.

units.zh: 阮元與長庚議夷艇高大，水師戰艦不能制，乃集捐十餘萬金付長庚，赴閩造大艦三十，名曰霆船，鑄大砲四百餘配之。
units.en: Ruan Yuan and Changgeng agreed that the foreign junks were too tall for the navy's warships to overcome, so they raised more than a hundred thousand taels in donations and entrusted them to Changgeng to build thirty large vessels in Fujian, called Thunder Ships, fitted with more than four hundred heavy cannon.
units.literal: Ruan Yuan and Changgeng discussed that the foreign junks were tall and the naval warships could not master them; they therefore raised more than a hundred thousand taels in donations for Changgeng to go to Fujian and build thirty large ships called Thunder Ships, casting more than four hundred great guns to equip them.

units.zh: 連敗牽等於海上，軍威大振。
units.en: He defeated Cai Qian and his allies again and again at sea, and the navy's prestige soared.
units.literal: He repeatedly defeated Qian and others at sea, and military prestige rose greatly.

units.zh: 八年，牽竄定海，進香普陀山，長庚掩至，牽僅以身免，窮追至閩洋，賊船糧盡帆壞，偽乞降於總督玉德，遣興泉永道慶徠赴三沙招撫，玉德遽檄浙師收港，牽得以其間修船揚帆去。
units.en: In the eighth year Cai Qian slipped into Dinghai to offer incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng surprised him, and Qian escaped only with his life. Changgeng pursued him into Fujian waters until the pirate fleet was out of provisions and its sails in tatters. Qian then feigned surrender to Governor-General Yude, who sent Circuit Intendant Qing Lai of Xing-Quan-Yong to Sansha to negotiate. Yude abruptly ordered the Zhejiang fleet back to harbor, and Qian used the respite to refit his ships and escape.
units.literal: In the eighth year Qian fled to Dinghai and went to burn incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng fell upon him by surprise and Qian barely escaped with his life; pursued to Fujian waters, the pirate ships ran out of grain and their sails were ruined; he falsely petitioned to surrender to Governor Yude, who sent Xing-Quan-Yong circuit intendant Qing Lai to Sansha to offer amnesty; Yude hastily ordered the Zhejiang fleet to withdraw to port, and Qian used the interval to repair his ships and sail away.

units.zh: 浙師追擊於三沙及溫州，毀其船六。
units.en: The Zhejiang fleet gave chase at Sansha and Wenzhou and destroyed six of his vessels.
units.literal: The Zhejiang fleet pursued and attacked at Sansha and Wenzhou, destroying six of his ships.

units.zh: 自乾隆季年，安南內亂，招瀕海亡命劫內洋，以濟餉為患，粵東土盜鳳尾、水澳兩幫附之，遂益肆擾。
units.en: In the closing years of Qianlong, civil war in Annam drew coastal outlaws to raid China's inner seas to raise funds, and the native Guangdong gangs known as Fengwei and Shui'ao joined them, so that piracy grew ever more rampant.
units.literal: From the late Qianlong period, Annam was torn by internal disorder and recruited coastal desperadoes to plunder the inner seas to supply funds, which became a scourge; the Guangdong native pirate bands Fengwei and Shui'ao attached themselves to them, and disturbances grew worse.

units.zh: 其在閩者，皆為漳盜蔡牽所並，有艇百餘，粵盜硃濆亦得數十艘。
units.en: Those who remained in Fujian were absorbed by the Zhangzhou pirate Cai Qian, who commanded more than a hundred junks, while the Guangdong pirate Zhu Fen acquired several dozen vessels of his own.
units.literal: Those remaining in Fujian were all absorbed by the Zhangzhou pirate Cai Qian, who had more than a hundred junks; the Guangdong pirate Zhu Fen also obtained several dozen vessels.

units.zh: 上諮鶚元，鶚元猶庇瑍不以實陳，乃遣尚書慶桂、侍郎王昶按治；
units.en: The emperor questioned Eyuan, who still shielded Yin and did not tell the truth. The emperor then sent Minister Qinggui and Vice Minister Wang Chang to investigate;
units.literal: The emperor questioned Eyuan; Eyuan still shielded Yin and did not report truthfully, whereupon Minister Qinggui and Vice Minister Wang Chang were dispatched to investigate;

units.zh: 三十九年，陝西巡撫畢沅、陝總督勒爾謹請如例收納監糧，允之。
units.en: In Qianlong 39, Shaanxi Governor Bi Yuan and Shaan-Gan Governor-General Le Erjin requested collecting academy grain as regulated; approval was granted.
units.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, Shaanxi Governor Bi Yuan and Shaan-Gan Governor-General Le Erjin requested collecting academy grain as per regulations; this was granted.

units.zh: 少有異禀，讀書目數行下，同郡錢陳群稱為異才。
units.en: As a boy he showed unusual talent and could read several lines at a glance; Qian Chenqun of his prefecture hailed him as a prodigy.
units.literal: In youth he possessed unusual gifts; when reading, his eye took in several lines at once; Qian Chenqun of the same commandery called him a prodigy.

units.zh: 乾隆二十七年，南巡，召試，賜舉人，授內閣中書。
units.en: In Qianlong 27, during the emperor's southern tour, he was summoned for a special examination, granted the rank of provincial graduate, and appointed drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
units.literal: In the 27th year of Qianlong, during the southern tour, he was summoned for examination, granted juren status, and appointed a Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat.

units.zh: 嘉慶元年，以福康安平苗功，贈貝子。
units.en: In 1796 Fukang'an's pacification of the Miao won Fu Heng a posthumous beizi rank.
units.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, because Fukang'an pacified the Miao, Fu Heng was posthumously given the rank of beizi.

units.zh: 福康安卒，推恩贈郡王銜，旋並命配享太廟。
units.en: After Fukang'an's death the family was raised to princely rank and granted shared sacrifice in the Ancestral Temple.
units.literal: When Fukang'an died, favor was extended to grant the posthumous rank of prince; soon he was also ordered to share sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 子福靈安、福隆安、福康安、福長安。
units.en: His sons were Fuling'an, Fulong'an, Fukang'an, and Fuchang'an.
units.literal: His sons were Fuling'an, Fulong'an, Fukang'an, and Fuchang'an.

units.zh: 福康安自有傳。
units.en: Fukang'an has a separate biography.
units.literal: Fukang'an has his own biography.

units.zh: 七月，卒，上親臨其第酹酒，命喪葬視宗室鎮國公，諡文忠。
units.en: In the seventh month he died; the emperor poured libation at his house, gave him a prince's funeral, and posthumous title Wenzhong.
units.literal: In the seventh month he died; the emperor personally visited his house to pour libation, ordered funeral rites equal to a clansman prince of the blood of the third degree, and gave the posthumous title Wenzhong.

units.zh: 世宗復以歲久積差，準監臣改用橢圓術。
units.en: Yongzheng, seeing accumulated error over the years, had supervising astronomers adopt elliptical theory.
units.literal: The Shizong Emperor again, because long years had accumulated discrepancy, ordered supervising officials to adopt the elliptical method.

units.zh: 有清統一區夏，聖聖相承。
units.en: The Qing unified China, one sage emperor following another.
units.literal: The Qing unified All-under-Heaven, sage succeeding sage.

units.zh: 設台站，令瑚爾起以七百人駐守。
units.en: Relay stations were set up and Hu Erqi garrisoned with 700 men.
units.literal: Relay stations were established and Hu Erqi was left with seven hundred men to garrison.

units.zh: 時傅恆及提督岳鍾琪決策深入，莎羅奔遣頭人乞降，傅恆令自縛詣軍門。
units.en: Fu Heng and Yue Zhongqi chose to push deep; Slob Dpon sent headmen to sue for peace, and Fu Heng ordered him to bind himself and come to camp.
units.literal: At that time Fu Heng and Commander Yue Zhongqi decided on deep penetration; Slob Dpon sent headmen to beg surrender, and Fu Heng ordered him to bind himself and come to headquarters.

units.zh: 三十四年，命大學士傅恆經略雲南軍務，高宗不升殿，不禮堂子，不祭纛，不親送。
units.en: In the thirty-fourth year, Grand Secretary Fu Heng was appointed grand coordinator for Yunnan military affairs; the Gaozong did not ascend the hall, did not perform rites at the tangzi, did not sacrifice to the battle standards, and did not personally send him off.
units.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, Grand Secretary Fu Heng was ordered as grand coordinator for Yunnan military affairs; the Gaozong did not ascend the hall, did not perform rites at the tangzi, did not sacrifice to the standards, and did not personally send him off.

units.zh: 內閣學士奉敕印至太和殿，經略等先俟陛階，大學士二人立殿外。
units.en: A Cabinet Academician brought the edict and seal to the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the grand coordinator and others waited first at the steps, while two grand secretaries stood outside the hall.
units.literal: A Cabinet Academician brought the edict and seal to the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the grand coordinator and others first waited at the steps; two grand secretaries stood outside the hall.

units.zh: 屆時經略升陛，印官從大閣學士入奉敕印出，經略跪受。
units.en: When the time came the grand coordinator ascended the steps; the seal officer, following the senior Cabinet Academician, entered and bore out the edict and seal, and the grand coordinator knelt to receive them.
units.literal: When the time came the grand coordinator ascended the steps; the seal officer, following the senior Cabinet Academician, entered, bore out the edict and seal, and the grand coordinator knelt to receive them.

units.zh: 禮畢，奉敕印官前，經略後，及階下，置敕印采亭內，前張黃蓋，列御仗，從征侍衛前引，餘俱後隨，至經略第止。
units.en: When the rites were completed, the bearer of the edict and seal went ahead and the grand coordinator followed; at the foot of the steps the edict and seal were placed in the colored canopy sedan; a yellow parasol was displayed in front, imperial guards were arrayed, expedition attendants led the way, and the rest followed behind, continuing until the grand coordinator's residence.
units.literal: When the rites were completed, the bearer of the edict and seal went ahead and the grand coordinator followed; at the foot of the steps they were placed in the colored canopy sedan; a yellow parasol was displayed in front, imperial guards were arrayed, expedition attendants led in front, and the rest followed behind, continuing until the grand coordinator's residence.

units.zh: 屆日肅隊行。
units.en: On the appointed day he set out with his ranks in formal order.
units.literal: On the appointed day he set out with his ranks in formal order.

units.zh: 敕印陳廳案上。
units.en: The edict and seal were displayed on the desk in the reception hall.
units.literal: The edict and seal were displayed on the desk in the reception hall.

units.zh: 師破東南木寨，緬兵夜自水寨出，傅恆令海蘭察御之，又令伊勒圖督舟師掩擊，复獲船纛。
units.en: Our troops took the southeast timber camp; the Burmese sallied by night from the water camp; Hailancha repelled them and Yiletui's fleet seized more boats and banners.
units.literal: The army broke the southeastern timber stockade; Burmese troops came out at night from the water stockade; Fu Heng ordered Hailancha to repel them and Yiletui to direct the fleet in a surprise attack, again capturing boats and banners.

units.zh: 三十四年二月，班師。
units.en: In the second month of 1769 the army withdrew.
units.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year the army withdrew.

units.zh: 三月，復命如山東會巡撫阿里袞治賑。
units.en: In the third month he was again sent to Shandong to join Governor Aligun in famine relief.
units.literal: In the third month he was again ordered to Shandong to join Governor Aligun in famine relief.

units.zh: 高宗又以舊記星紀，間有疏漏，御製璣衡撫辰儀，重加測候。
units.en: Qianlong, finding gaps in older star catalogs, built the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and remeasured the sky.
units.literal: The Gaozong Emperor again, because old star records had occasional gaps, personally made the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and took new observations.

units.zh: 乾隆六十年以後，國史無徵，則從闕焉。
units.en: After Qianlong 60 the Veritable Records offer no material, so the account stops there.
units.literal: After Qianlong year 60 the National History has no testimony, and those years are therefore omitted.

units.zh: 今以康熙年間實測各省及諸蒙古高度、偏度，並乾隆時憲所增省分，與回疆部落、兩金川土司等，晝夜永短，節氣早晚，推得高度、偏度備列焉。
units.en: Here Kangxi surveys, Qianlong additions, Xinjiang, and Jinchuan observations yield revised polar altitudes and longitudinal offsets.
units.literal: Now from Kangxi-era actual surveys of each province and Mongol banners, plus provinces added in the Qianlong Time Constitution, together with Muslim borderland tribes and the two Jinchuan chieftaincies — day and night length, solar-term timing — heights and offsets are derived and fully listed.

units.zh: 迨平定回疆及兩金川，復令重度裏差，增入時憲。
units.en: After pacifying Xinjiang and the two Jinchuan campaigns, he ordered li-cha remeasured and entered into the Shixian calendar.
units.literal: When the Muslim borderlands and the Two Jinchuan were pacified, he again ordered remeasurement of li-cha and added the results to the Time Constitution calendar.

units.zh: 服闋待次，時平涼回酋田五作亂，爾漢與通判吳廷芳、知縣黃家駒守靖遠城，賊來攻。
units.en: After mourning he waited for a new posting. The Muslim leader Tian Wu of Pingliang had risen in revolt, and Erhan, together with Subprefect Wu Tingfang and Magistrate Huang Jiaju, held Jingyuan when the rebels assaulted the walls.
units.literal: When mourning ended he awaited appointment; at that time the Pingliang Muslim chief Tian Wu rebelled. Erhan, with subprefect Wu Tingfang and magistrate Huang Jiaju, defended Jingyuan city as bandits came to attack.

units.zh: 乾隆中，官甘肅靖遠典史，母憂去官。
units.en: Under Qianlong he held the post of registrar at Jingyuan in Gansu, then left office to observe mourning for his mother.
units.literal: In the Qianlong era he served as registrar of Jingyuan, Gansu, and left office on his mother's death.

units.zh: 胡振聲，亦同安人，提督貴子。
units.en: Hu Zhensheng, also from Tong'an, was the son of Commander-in-Chief Hu Gui.
units.literal: Hu Zhensheng was also a man of Tong'an, a son of Commander-in-Chief Gui.

units.zh: 盧焯圖爾炳阿阿思哈宮兆麟楊景素閔鶚元
units.en: Lu Chao, Tu Erbing'a, Asiha, Gong Zhaolin, Yang Jingsu, and Min Eyuan
units.literal: Lu Chao, Tu Erbing'a, Asiha, Gong Zhaolin, Yang Jingsu, Min Eyuan

units.zh: 楊景素，字樸園，江南甘泉人，提督捷孫。
units.en: Yang Jingsu, styled Puyuan, was from Ganquan in Jiangnan and grandson of Grand Coordinator Jie.
units.literal: Yang Jingsu, courtesy name Puyuan, was a native of Ganquan in Jiangnan, grandson of Grand Coordinator Jie.

units.zh: 乾隆三年，補蠡縣縣丞，累遷保定知府。
units.en: In 1738 he became assistant magistrate of Li County and rose through successive posts to prefect of Baoding.
units.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was appointed county assistant magistrate of Li County, and through successive promotions reached prefect of Baoding.

units.zh: 十八年，授福建汀漳龍道。
units.en: In 1753 he was appointed intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long circuit in Fujian.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed intendant of Ting-Zhang-Long in Fujian.

units.zh: 三十三年，授河南按察使。
units.en: In 1768 he was appointed provincial judge of Henan.
units.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed provincial judge of Henan.

units.zh: 三十五年，擢甘肅布政使，調直隸。
units.en: In 1770 he became treasurer of Gansu and was transferred to Zhili.
units.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was promoted provincial treasurer of Gansu and transferred to Zhili.

units.zh: 三十九年，壽張民王倫為亂，大學士舒赫德督兵討之。
units.en: In 1774 Wang Lun led a rebellion in Shouzhang; Grand Secretary Suhede took command against him.
units.literal: In the thirty-ninth year commoners of Shouzhang, Wang Lun, rebelled; Grand Secretary Suhede commanded troops to suppress them.

units.zh: 四十年，疏請選京師健銳、火器營裨佐發山東，司營伍教演。
units.en: In 1775 he asked that adjutants from the capital's Elite and Firearms brigades be sent to Shandong to train local garrisons.
units.literal: In the fortieth year he memorialized requesting selection of adjutants from the capital's Elite and Firearms brigades to be sent to Shandong to manage camp drill and instruction.

units.zh: 四十一年，上東巡，臨視臨清毀橋斷道及亂民竄據所在，景素述當時戰狀，上嘉其勞，賜黃馬褂。
units.en: During the 1776 eastern tour the emperor inspected Linqing, where bridges had been destroyed and rebels had held ground. Jingsu described the fighting; the emperor praised his service and granted him a yellow jacket.
units.literal: In the forty-first year, during the emperor's eastern tour, he personally viewed the destroyed bridges and severed roads at Linqing and where rebels had lurked; Jingsu narrated the fighting at the time; the emperor praised his labors and granted a yellow jacket.

units.zh: 四十二年，景素奏請濬舊渠，並開支河二，令仍趨南陽、昭陽二湖，下部議行。
units.en: In 1777 he asked to dredge the old canal and cut two branch channels to restore flow to Nanyang and Zhaoyang lakes. The ministries approved.
units.literal: In the forty-second year Jingsu memorialized requesting dredging of the old canal and opening two branch channels so water would again flow toward Nanyang and Zhaoyang lakes; the memorial was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

units.zh: 擢兩廣總督，四十三年，調閩浙。
units.en: He was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi, then in 1778 transferred to Fujian and Zhejiang.
units.literal: He was promoted governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi; in the forty-third year he was transferred to Fujian and Zhejiang.

units.zh: 四十四年，調直隸。
units.en: In 1779 he was transferred to Zhili.
units.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was transferred to Zhili.

units.zh: 四十五年，兩廣總督巴延三奏景素操守不謹，並發官兵得贓縱盜狀。
units.en: In 1780 Governor-General Bayansan reported that Jingsu had been lax in integrity and that his troops had taken bribes and released bandits.
units.literal: In the forty-fifth year Guangdong-Guangxi Governor-General Bayansan memorialized that Jingsu's conduct had not been scrupulous and also exposed soldiers' acceptance of bribes and release of bandits.

units.zh: 五十四年，以福建吏治廢弛，追咎景素，戍召伊犁。
units.en: In 1789, citing slack Fujian governance, the emperor held the late Jingsu accountable and exiled his son Zhao to Ili.
units.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, citing the slackening of Fujian official discipline, Jingsu was held accountable retroactively and exiled to Ili.

units.zh: 景素孱弱，不好章句，貧不能自給。
units.en: Jingsu was sickly, had no taste for classical scholarship, and was too poor to support himself.
units.literal: Jingsu was frail and weak, disliked textual study, and in poverty could not support himself.

units.zh: 入貲授縣丞，發直隸河工效力。
units.en: He bought his way into office as a county assistant magistrate and was assigned to Zhili river works.
units.literal: He entered office by purchase of rank as county assistant magistrate and was sent to serve on Zhili river works.

units.zh: 漳浦民蔡榮祖欲為亂，景素率營卒擒斬之。
units.en: When Zhangpu commoner Cai Rongzu plotted rebellion, Jingsu led garrison troops to capture and execute him.
units.literal: A commoner of Zhangpu, Cai Rongzu, intended to rebel; Jingsu led camp soldiers to capture and execute him.

units.zh: 調台灣道。
units.en: He was transferred to Taiwan circuit.
units.literal: He was transferred to Taiwan circuit.

units.zh: 釐定漢民墾種地，並生熟番界址。
units.en: He fixed the boundaries of Han settlers' reclaimed land and the frontier between raw and acculturated aboriginal peoples.
units.literal: He fixed boundaries of Han reclaimed land and of raw and acculturated aboriginal territories.

units.zh: 革遊民為通譯而不法者，代以熟番。
units.en: He removed lawless Han vagrants who worked as interpreters and replaced them with acculturated aborigines.
units.literal: He eliminated indigent Han who served as interpreters but acted lawlessly, replacing them with acculturated aborigines.

units.zh: 又禁入山採木，借修造戰船材料為名，累諸番。
units.en: He also banned timber gathering in the hills under the pretext of supplying warship repairs, a burden long imposed on the aborigines.
units.literal: He also forbade entering the mountains to cut timber under the pretext of gathering materials to repair and build war vessels, which had burdened the aborigines.

units.zh: 坐失察雄縣知縣胡錫瑛侵蝕災賑，下吏議，奪官，命留任，俟八年無過，方准開復。
units.en: He was stripped of rank for failing to detect Xiong County magistrate Hu Xiying's embezzlement of disaster relief, but allowed to remain in office; restoration would come only after eight years without fault.
units.literal: For failure to detect Xiong County magistrate Hu Xiying's embezzlement of disaster relief, the case was referred to officials; his office was stripped but he was ordered to remain in post, and only after eight years without fault would restoration be permitted.

units.zh: 上命景素具車馬濟師，令分守河西。
units.en: The emperor ordered Jingsu to supply transport for the army and hold the west bank of the river.
units.literal: The emperor ordered Jingsu to provide carts and horses to aid the army and commanded him to hold the west bank of the river separately.

units.zh: 賊以糧艘結浮橋欲渡，景素與總兵萬朝興、副將瑪爾當阿等督兵御之，董勸回民助師。
units.en: The rebels lashed grain boats into a pontoon to cross the river. Jingsu, Brigadier Wan Chaoxing, Deputy Commander Ma'erdang'a, and others held them off and rallied local Muslims to support the army.
units.literal: The rebels joined grain boats into a pontoon bridge to cross; Jingsu with Brigadier Wan Chaoxing, Deputy Commander Ma'erdang'a, and others commanded troops to resist, and urged Hui people to assist the army.

units.zh: 夜焚橋，賊不得渡。
units.en: They burned the bridge by night and kept the rebels from crossing.
units.literal: At night they burned the bridge, and the rebels could not cross.

units.zh: 事旋定，擢山東巡撫。
units.en: After the rebellion was crushed he was promoted governor of Shandong.
units.literal: Matters were soon settled, and he was promoted governor of Shandong.

units.zh: 疏請編查保甲。
units.en: He memorialized asking to compile and inspect baojia registers.
units.literal: He memorialized requesting compilation and inspection of baojia household registers.

units.zh: 疏言：「浙西歉收，總督楊廷璋請撥台灣倉穀十萬接濟。
units.en: He memorialized: 'Western Zhejiang had a poor harvest. Governor-General Yang Tingzhang asked to draw 100,000 shi of grain from Taiwan's granaries for relief.
units.literal: He memorialized: 'Western Zhejiang suffered poor harvest; Governor-General Yang Tingzhang requested allocation of one hundred thousand shi of Taiwan granary grain for relief.

units.zh: 北風盛發，未能即到。
units.en: Strong north winds would delay shipment.
units.literal: North winds were strong and the grain could not arrive immediately.

units.zh: 請於福州、福寧、興化、泉州四府屬撥倉穀十萬，聽商運赴嘉、湖出糶；
units.en: He proposed releasing 100,000 shi from granaries in Fuzhou, Funing, Xinghua, and Quanzhou and letting merchants haul it to Jiaxing and Huzhou for relief sales;
units.literal: He requested that one hundred thousand shi of granary grain be drawn from the four prefectures of Fuzhou, Funing, Xinghua, and Quanzhou, allowing merchants to transport it to Jiaxing and Huzhou for sale as relief;

units.zh: 仍飭台灣運歸四府補倉。」
units.en: Taiwan's granaries would later be restocked to replace the four prefectures' reserves.'
units.literal: Taiwan grain was still to be ordered transported back to replenish the four prefectures' granaries.'

units.zh: 十二月，卒，贈太子太保，賜卹如例。
units.en: He died in the twelfth month and was posthumously named Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the usual mourning honors.
units.literal: In the twelfth month he died; he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and bereavement grants were awarded according to precedent.

units.zh: 福康安又奏景素在兩廣婪索商捐六萬餘，責景素子炤限年繳還。
units.en: Fuk'anggan also reported that Jingsu had extorted over 60,000 in merchant levies in Guangdong and Guangxi; his son Zhao was ordered to repay within a fixed term.
units.literal: Fuk'anggan further memorialized that Jingsu in Guangdong-Guangxi had greedily extorted more than sixty thousand in merchant levies; Jingsu's son Zhao was ordered to repay within a set term.

units.zh: 論曰：法者所以持天下之平。
units.en: The historians comment: Law exists to uphold fairness in the realm.
units.literal: The commentary says: Law is what upholds fairness under Heaven.

units.zh: 焯、阿思哈、景素坐貪皆勘實，猶尚復起；
units.en: Chao, Asiha, and Jingsu were all convicted of corruption on solid evidence, yet were restored to office;
units.literal: Chao, Asiha, and Jingsu were all convicted of greed with substantiated investigations, yet were still restored;
